name: Dialpad
description: Dialpad is an AI-powered customer communications platform that brings calling, messaging, meetings, support, and contact-center workflows into one service. Organizations use it to connect teams and customers, operate business phone systems, manage conversations, and apply real-time communications intelligence.
agentUseSummary: Connect one Dialpad user with Relay-owned confidential S256 PKCE OAuth, then let agents verify that exact user and inspect at most ten deduplicated privacy-masked Caller ID choices without exposing provider identity, email, extension, organization metadata, forwarding numbers, communications, special scopes, administration, writes, pagination, or raw APIs.

credentialRequirements.label: Dialpad OAuth client ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Railway-held client ID for an approved Dialpad OAuth app requesting only the additional offline_access scope.

credentialRequirements.name: DIALPAD_CLIENT_SECRET
credentialRequirements.label: Dialpad OAuth client secret
credentialRequirements.helpText: Railway-encrypted confidential OAuth secret used for code and refresh exchanges; never entered in Relay Console clients.

capabilities.description: Verify the exact OAuth-bound Dialpad user without exposing provider IDs, email, extension, organization, or status metadata.

capabilities.label: Read caller-ID choices

allowed.label: Verify connected user
allowed.description: Verify the exact OAuth-bound Dialpad user without returning provider identity.

allowed.label: Read caller-ID choices
allowed.description: Read at most ten deduplicated privacy-masked own-user Caller ID choices from the current provider schema without forwarding numbers.

blocked.label: Block identity, organization, and administration
blocked.description: Provider user ID, email, extension, state, license, company, office, groups, directories, voicemail settings, app settings, and administration are unavailable.

blocked.label: Block communications and sensitive artifacts
blocked.description: Calls, callbacks, SMS, fax, recordings, transcripts, messages, voicemail, forwarding numbers, routing, contacts, contact-center data, and every communication action are unavailable.

blocked.label: Block special scopes, other products, and raw access
blocked.description: calls:list, recordings_export, message exports, screen_pop, change_log, devices, events, webhooks, websockets, AI products, sandbox, pagination, exports, writes, and raw APIs are unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The two selected fixed reads run automatically; provider identity, forwarding numbers, communications, special scopes, organization data, writes, and raw APIs remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same two reads run without Relay per-action approval; exact user binding, fixed routes, response bounds, audits, masking, and secret isolation still apply.

providerSetup.blocker: Approved Dialpad OAuth access, exact Railway callback, credentials, API-terms/privacy/brand review, representative user account, consent, any provider marketplace review, and staging validation remain for separate authorized tasks.
providerSetup.nextAction: After batch integration, request or review Dialpad OAuth access, register the exact Railway callback, store credentials in staging, and validate state, S256 PKCE, exact additional offline_access scope, confidential code exchange, rotating refresh replacement, exact user binding, sensitive metadata exclusion, current Caller ID schema, forwarding-number exclusion, response limits, rate-limit handling, upstream deauthorization, local deletion, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Dialpad presents an AI-powered customer communications platform spanning calling, messaging, meetings, support, contact-center workflows, and communications intelligence.

Dialpad documents confidential authorization-code OAuth, production authorization and token endpoints, state, S256 PKCE, offline_access refresh tokens, rotating refresh exchange, special scopes Relay excludes, self-user validation, and bearer deauthorization.
Dialpad recommends Bearer authorization headers and documents authentication boundaries Relay keeps server-side.
Dialpad documents the User Get route with the me identifier and sensitive identity, contact, organization, status, license, voicemail, and group fields Relay excludes from agent-visible output.

Dialpad's current Caller ID response schema exposes caller_id, primary_phone, phone_numbers, office_main_line, groups, and forwarding_numbers; Relay masks and bounds the first four candidate sources and excludes forwarding_numbers.
Dialpad documents company and endpoint-specific limits and HTTP 429 behavior; Relay performs one request per action and does not retry automatically.
Dialpad publishes API Terms of Service and privacy terms governing API registration, credentials, end-user data, branding, and use, so live release remains externally gated.
